summary: Sub-fix 7.3.A applied successfully (SessionView.tsx wiring correction — the spec's 'smoking gun'). Sub-fixes 7.3.B and 7.3.C blocked by pre-existing quality-gate hook violation on sync.ts (file is 2418 lines, hook ceiling is 800). Per CLAUDE.md Subagent Hook Discipline, blocked operations are reported, not bypassed. Spec Section 7 explicitly anticipated this risk ('files >800 lines... may hit pretool-quality-gate.py'). Refactoring sync.ts to <800 lines would be a 1600+-line surgery, violating the Minimum-Diff Rule by 80x and out of scope for this pipeline.

sub_fixes_applied.summary: Added useSocketStatus to imports. Replaced useLayoutEffect dependency [sessionId, realtimeStatus] with [sessionId, socketStatus] so visible-session catch-up runs on websocket reconnect (not on voice realtime status change, which was the prior broken wiring per Codex H_E). Kept realtimeStatus binding for mic button (different concern). Added a 4-line comment explaining the change and pointing at spec §5.19 / pipeline 7.3.

sub_fixes_blocked.intended_lines: ~229-240 (onSessionVisible adds lastVisibleSessionId tracking), class-level field, ~1756-1771 (reconnect callback)
sub_fixes_blocked.block_reason: pretool-quality-gate.py rejects all edits to sync.ts because the file is 2418 lines (max 800). This is a pre-existing structural condition — not introduced by this pipeline. Hook scans whole-file post-edit content, so even a 1-line addition triggers the same block.
sub_fixes_blocked.harmonization_with_7.3.A: 7.3.A binds visible-session catch-up to socketStatus in SessionView (the React-component path); 7.3.B does it from the sync side (the data-layer path). Either works in isolation; both shipped is defence-in-depth and matches the spec's 'redundant safety nets' guidance.

sub_fixes_blocked.block_reason: Same structural block as 7.3.B — pretool-quality-gate.py rejects all sync.ts edits.
sub_fixes_blocked.logic_chosen: Conservative preserve-if-recent: only preserve when (a) we already had thinking=true in local state (so we are not fabricating thinking on a clean boot), AND (b) server's activeAt is within 5s (so CLI is plausibly still active). This is robust regardless of whether Pipeline 7.2 lands a snapshot.
sub_fixes_blocked.harmonization_with_7.2:
Conservative — works whether or not 7.2 ships a thinking snapshot on connect:
  - If 7.2 ships: snapshot arrives within ~1s of connect; our 5s preserve window bridges that gap, then snapshot overwrites (no UI flash).
  - If 7.2 misses: 5s preserve gives the CLI's next 2s session-alive ephemeral time to arrive (CLI heartbeat is volatile.emit every 2s per packages/happy-cli/src/claude/session.ts:69-73).
  - If session truly idle: activeAt is older than 5s, preserve=false, reset behaviour matches current code.
A follow-up cycle can tighten the window once 7.2's behaviour is verified.

scope_review_note: Layer matches BA's diagnosis_layer L4 (data-flow wiring / state-machine state distribution). I am not requesting a layer change; I am reporting a hook-induced partial block. This is the same kind of partial block the spec Section 7 anticipated.
harmonization_with_pipelines_7.1_and_7.2: 7.3.A alone meaningfully improves Layer 2 recovery: when websocket reconnects, the visible session re-fetches via REST (catches messages that arrived during disconnect). It does NOT solve the 'thinking' indicator — that needs 7.3.C (preserve-if-recent on hydrate) and/or 7.2 (server snapshot on connect). Without 7.3.B, the catch-up only fires when a SessionView is mounted (i.e., user is looking at a session); a backgrounded tab that reconnects won't catch up until the user navigates to the session — but 7.3.A's socketStatus dependency causes the next visible-session render to re-fetch, so a tab refresh / navigation back to the session is sufficient. The 'real-time' AC1 (no user action needed) is partially addressed by 7.3.A in the common 'tab visible during reconnect' case.

diff_stats.justification_for_overage: 1 line for the import addition + 1 line for new useSocketStatus() hook call + 1 line for changed dependency array + 4 lines of explanatory comment pointing at spec §5.19 / pipeline 7.3. Comment is justified because the prior wiring had a misleading comment (sync.ts:1765-1767 'SessionView re-fetches on realtimeStatus change') that contributed to the original bug; future readers need explicit pointer to the corrected wiring.

ready_for_qa_caveat: QA may verify 7.3.A in isolation. Full AC verification (AC1 real-time bg-task render, AC2 reopen-state-restore, AC3 timestamp-not-frozen) requires 7.1, 7.2, and the blocked 7.3.B+C to all land. 7.3.A alone fixes the 'visible session catch-up after reconnect' subset of the bug.

options_for_user: Option 1 (recommended): Accept 7.3.A as the primary fix. Defer 7.3.B (defence in depth) and 7.3.C (hydrate preserve) to a follow-up cycle that first refactors sync.ts into smaller modules. The spec already lists the partial-fix path as acceptable.
Option 2: Authorise a one-time hook bypass for this specific sync.ts edit. User runs the edit manually with the diffs included in this report.
Option 3: Spawn a separate Dev pipeline 7.4 'split sync.ts into modules' (a ~1600-line refactor) and then re-run 7.3.B + 7.3.C against the smaller resulting file. Out of scope for this pipeline.

evidence_capture_notes_for_qa:
Per BA spec R3 (runtime-evidence requirement) and addendum AC5: QA must capture, during a reproduction:
  1. Browser DevTools WebSocket frames showing /v1/updates connect.
  2. Whether the visible-session triggers a /v3/sessions/:id/messages?after_seq=... call within 1s of socket reconnect (this is what 7.3.A enables).
  3. Whether 'claude babbling' indicator returns. With ONLY 7.3.A landed, expect: messages catch up but indicator remains 'online' until next CLI session-alive (~2s). With 7.3.C also landed: indicator is preserved across reopen if activeAt is recent. With 7.2 also landed: indicator is restored from server snapshot.
